html:
On 5 June 1849 King Frederick VII signed the first democratic constitution of Denmark, ending nearly two centuries of absolute monarchy.

In March 1848, as revolutions swept Europe, crowds marched to the palace in Copenhagen and the new king agreed to give up absolute power. An assembly drew up a constitution with a two-chamber parliament, freedom of the press and of religion, and the vote for most men over thirty.

5 June is Constitution Day in Denmark. The constitution was revised several times; women won the vote in 1915, and the version of 1953 is in force. Its quarrels with the Schleswig question shaped the next decades, and the free farmers made by the end of the Stavnsbånd became its backbone.
sum: On 5 June 1849 King Frederick VII signed the first democratic constitution of Denmark, ending nearly two centuries of absolute monarchy.
